issues.issue: Whether the H&C officer could decide that removal would breach Canadian law, as the judge suggested
issues.applicant_position: Minister: the s. 25 officer's jurisdiction is limited to H&C considerations, not validity of removal.
issues.respondent_position: Officer must consider the ICCPR and other international law arguments in the H&C application.
issues.result_quote: is limited to decide whether H&C considerations justify exempting the respondent

issues.issue: Whether the officer dealt adequately with the ICCPR-based family and child interests in the H&C decision
issues.applicant_position: Minister: officer addressed the substance of the child and family interests; judge should not have intervened.
issues.respondent_position: Officer had to consider the ICCPR family and child arguments; refusing to do so breached fairness.
issues.result_quote: it is clear that she addressed in substance the different and important interests at stake

issues.issue: Whether the officer's refusal to consider the ICCPR arguments denied the respondent a fair hearing
issues.applicant_position: Minister: no unfairness; officer's reasons addressed the substance of the issues.
issues.respondent_position: Officer had to consider all arguments; refusing some breached audi alteram partem.
issues.result_quote: it becomes unnecessary to address the Applications Judge

issues.issue: Whether the certified question (jurisdiction to consider ICCPR breach under s. 25) should be answered
issues.applicant_position: Minister: question is irrelevant and not dispositive of the appeal.
issues.respondent_position: Proposed a narrower certified question on family-life and child guarantees in the ICCPR.
issues.result_quote: The certified question being irrelevant and not dispositive of this appeal
